title: Too many open files in system error (126) and forkpty(3) failure during high-volume shell command execution.

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a detailed bug report describing system file descriptor and process limit exhaustion ('Too many open files' Exit Code 126 and 'forkpty(3) failed') during high-volume shell command and sub-agent execution, along with complete environment and version information.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Addressing pseudo-terminal (PTY) file descriptor leaks and process limit exhaustion during high-volume shell executions involves node-pty process lifecycle management, signal/stream cleanup, and process group handling in ShellExecutionService. According to the effort estimation guidelines, platform-specific issues involving node-pty, child_process.spawn, and pseudo-terminal exhaustion are classified as LARGE effort.

summary.problem: High-volume shell command and sub-agent task execution exhausts system file descriptors and pseudo-terminals, resulting in Exit Code 126 ('Too many open files in system') and subsequent 'forkpty(3) failed' errors.
summary.root_cause: During rapid or high-volume shell tool executions, master/slave file descriptors from node-pty instances and write streams for background logs are not aggressively closed or garbage collected upon process completion or abortion, accumulating open descriptors until OS EMFILE/ENFILE limits are hit.
summary.context: Executing batch operations or parallel sub-agent workflows in large workspaces creates a heavy stream of shell tool invocations. Without strict cleanup and descriptor release in ShellExecutionService, the process reaches its open file descriptor limit.

steps: Ensure destroyPtyProcess and cleanupPtyEntry are called reliably on all exit, error, and abort paths in executeWithPty.
Ensure background log streams and file descriptors in backgroundLogStreams are promptly closed and removed when processes terminate or are cleaned up.
Add error handling for EMFILE/ENFILE errors during PTY spawning to gracefully fall back to child_process or surface actionable diagnostic error messages.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Executing high volumes of shell commands in rapid succession closes all associated file descriptors and PTY processes without triggering descriptor leaks or forkpty failures.
verification_steps: Add a test in shellExecutionService.test.ts that executes a rapid sequence of shell commands using PTY execution.
Verify that activePtys, activeChildProcesses, and backgroundLogStreams are completely cleared and all streams closed after completion.
Verify that process aborts clean up PTY descriptors immediately without orphan leaks.
